keyVerseText: Among all this people there were seven hundred chosen men lefthanded ; every one could sling stones at an hair breadth, and not miss.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun שַׂעֲרָה (saʻărâh) is the feminine form of שֵׂעָר (sêʻâr), which fundamentally denotes hair, especially with a sense of hairiness or the texture of hair. This root carries the idea not only of individual hairs but also the collective quality of hair, sometimes implying roughness or bristling. The literal sense of a single hair or the hairiness adds a tangible, detailed dimension beyond the English word 'hair,' emphasizing the distinctness and delicacy of each strand as well as the fullness of hair collectively.
usageInScripture: The word שַׂעֲרָה appears seven times in the Hebrew Bible, consistently referring to hair either as a singular strand or as a collective mass. Its translations range from 'a single hair' to 'the hairs,' showing both individual and plural uses. Phrases like 'there shall not one hair' and 'at a hair' demonstrate its use in precise, often figurative expressions, indicating extreme minuteness or exactness. This consistency reveals the word's role in conveying both physical detail and metaphorical precision.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding שַׂעֲרָה in its original Hebrew enriches our appreciation of God's intimate knowledge and care for His creation. The specificity of 'a single hair' reflects the biblical theme that God is aware of even the smallest details of our lives, underscoring His omniscience and providence. This word reminds believers of the value and dignity God places on each person, down to the finest detail, which is ultimately fulfilled in Christ's redeeming work. It also speaks to the precision and faithfulness of God's promises, as nothing escapes His sovereign control, not even a single hair.
keyVerseReflection: Judges 20:16 highlights the exceptional skill of seven hundred chosen men who could sling stones with such accuracy that they would not miss 'an hair breadth.' The use of שַׂעֲרָה here emphasizes the extreme precision and delicacy of their aim, illustrating a remarkable level of human ability granted by God. This verse, through the word שַׂעֲרָה, invites reflection on God's empowerment of His people to accomplish extraordinary feats, even those requiring meticulous exactness.
